design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks for one thing, to authorize the hard inquiry on his pending increase request. The limit he gets is fixed by line_ext_limit_increase only after three items that sit silently in the ledger are put right: a fee-bearing R02 return with no returned-payment fee, the most recent draw posted with no draw fee, and the replacement relief due on the fee of a return that the borrower replaced. Each of the four computations has five factors, every one moves its result on this world, and two of them read the borrower's personal loan.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims line_ext_close_to_draws_payment, line_ext_late_fee, line_ext_limit_review, line_ext_workout_fee_relief; this task claims line_ext_returned_payment_fee, line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee, line_ext_returned_fee_relief, line_ext_limit_increase with tools assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d, assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c, grant_returned_fee_relief_6fbb0f32, authorize_limit_increase_21546d5b; nothing is left for a later task. The two scopes are disjoint and together cover all eight extended policies.

DEPENDENCY CHAIN. Surface goal (authorize the inquiry) -> line_evt_limit_changes as overwritten by line_ext_limit_increase (amount set by the paragraph) -> four shares read from the ledger and the loan -> usage share reads the ledger total, so the fee (+), the draw fee (+) and the relief (-) must be on the ledger first -> the relief itself is figured from the fee (line_ext_returned_fee_relief <- line_ext_returned_payment_fee).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root line_ext_limit_increase (owner user, tool authorize_limit_increase_21546d5b). Prerequisites: line_ext_returned_payment_fee (assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d, agent), line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee (assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c, agent), line_ext_returned_fee_relief (grant_returned_fee_relief_6fbb0f32, agent).
Edge line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_returned_payment_fee: kind value_input, gate returned_fee_share, form state; policy_source "The approved limit is fixed only after every returned payment on the line whose return code carries a fee shows its returned-payment fee entry."; condition "Every line_payment_returned entry on the line whose return code is in the tier's fee_bearing_return_codes is the related entry of a line_returned_payment_fee_assessed entry."; false at the opening because The 2026-09-16 return carries code R02, which is in the FlexLine Plus fee_bearing_return_codes, and no line_returned_payment_fee_assessed entry on the line has it as its related entry. (initial_state.line_transactions.60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673.return_code = R02; initial_state.line_transactions.60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673.event_type = line_payment_returned); resolved by assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d: Step 9 books the fee entry (16.35) against that return; the returned-fee entries in 12 months become 1 and the returned-fee share moves from 1.00 to 0.75.
Edge line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee: kind value_input, gate recent_draw_charges, form state; policy_source "The approved limit is not fixed until each draw on the line carries a draw-fee entry, wherever the tier charges a draw fee."; condition "On a tier whose draw fee percent is above 0.00, every line_draw_posted entry on the line is the related entry of a line_draw_fee_assessed entry."; false at the opening because The FlexLine Plus draw fee percent is 2.0, and the 2026-09-10 draw 3535d23f-bfe7-4f46-b45d-e5f80debd090 is the related entry of no line_draw_fee_assessed entry. (initial_state.line_transactions.3535d23f-bfe7-4f46-b45d-e5f80debd090.event_type = line_draw_posted; initial_state.credit_lines.b2db4d01-9c63-44e2-8662-5e6f9185e430.variant_name = FlexLine Plus); resolved by assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c: Step 11 books the draw fee (18.27) against that draw; the draw charges of the last 3 months rise to 5,213.07, at least 65 percent of the limit, and the draw-intensity share moves from 0.90 to 0.80.
Edge line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_returned_fee_relief: kind value_input, gate usage_balance, form state; policy_source "The approved limit is fixed only after the returned-payment fee of a return that has a replacement payment recorded against it carries a courtesy fee-waiver entry."; condition "When the line's most recent returned payment has a payment recorded against it as its replacement and a returned-payment fee booked against it, a line_fee_waived entry with waiver_reason courtesy whose related entry is that fee exists."; false at the opening because The 2026-09-16 return has the payment 7d9789f9-4f17-4b7f-bc38-e1b6e9c1960c recorded against it as its replacement; once its fee is booked no line_fee_waived entry is tied to that fee (no fee waiver exists on the line at all). (initial_state.line_transactions.7d9789f9-4f17-4b7f-bc38-e1b6e9c1960c.related_txn_id = 60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673; initial_state.line_transactions.7d9789f9-4f17-4b7f-bc38-e1b6e9c1960c.event_type = line_payment_posted); resolved by grant_returned_fee_relief_6fbb0f32: Step 13 books the relief (6.12) against the fee of step 9; the ledger total falls from 6,403.25 to 6,397.13 and the usage share moves from 0.60 to 0.80.
Edge line_ext_returned_fee_relief -> line_ext_returned_payment_fee: kind value_input, gate relieved_fee, form state; policy_source "Replacement relief is fixed only after the returned payment it is for carries its returned-payment fee entry."; condition "The line's most recent line_payment_returned entry, whose return code is in the tier's fee_bearing_return_codes, is the related entry of a line_returned_payment_fee_assessed entry."; false at the opening because The latest return 60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673 (code R02) has no returned-payment fee entry, so there is no fee for the relief to start from. (initial_state.line_transactions.60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673.return_code = R02; initial_state.line_transactions.60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673.related_txn_id = 0d9dad4f-23ea-4784-b135-b761a0b3b3b7); resolved by assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d: Step 9 books the fee; relieved_fee becomes 16.35 and the relief basis is figured from it.
Topological order: line_ext_returned_payment_fee -> line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee -> line_ext_returned_fee_relief -> line_ext_limit_increase. Parallel edges: Edges: root <- returned-payment fee, root <- back-billed draw fee, root <- replacement relief, replacement relief <- returned-payment fee. The relief must follow the fee it is booked against, as its own prerequisite sentence says: "Replacement relief is fixed only after the returned payment it is for carries its returned-payment fee entry." The back-billed draw fee commutes with both: it reads the line's draws, limit and age, none of which the fee or the relief writes, and they read no draw or draw-fee entry. Every admissible order was replayed: returned_payment_fee -> backbilled_draw_fee -> returned_fee_relief: returned_payment_fee 16.35, backbilled_draw_fee 18.27, returned_fee_relief 6.12, limit_increase 8,800.00; terminal credit_limit 8,800.00, balance 6,397.13 | returned_payment_fee -> returned_fee_relief -> backbilled_draw_fee: returned_payment_fee 16.35, returned_fee_relief 6.12, backbilled_draw_fee 18.27, limit_increase 8,800.00; terminal credit_limit 8,800.00, balance 6,397.13 | backbilled_draw_fee -> returned_payment_fee -> returned_fee_relief: backbilled_draw_fee 18.27, returned_payment_fee 16.35, returned_fee_relief 6.12, limit_increase 8,800.00; terminal credit_limit 8,800.00, balance 6,397.13. All three leave the same scored arguments and the same terminal state.
Deletion sensitivity (each prerequisite write skipped, everything else replayed): line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_returned_payment_fee: Skipping the returned-payment fee leaves no returned-fee entry in 12 months (share 1.00) and no fee for the relief to start from (relief 0.00, nothing booked); the approved limit becomes 9,100.00 instead of 8,800.00. | line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee: Skipping the back-billed draw fee leaves the 2026-09-10 draw without a draw-fee entry in the terminal state and the terminal balance 6,378.86 instead of 6,397.13; the draw charges of the last 3 months stay at 5,194.80, below 65 percent of the limit, so the draw-intensity share is 0.90 and the approved limit becomes 8,900.00 instead of 8,800.00. | line_ext_limit_increase -> line_ext_returned_fee_relief: Skipping the replacement relief leaves the ledger total at 6,403.25, above 80 percent of the limit; the usage share falls to 0.60 and the approved limit becomes 8,600.00 instead of 8,800.00. | line_ext_returned_fee_relief -> line_ext_returned_payment_fee: Skipping the returned-payment fee leaves relieved_fee 0.00, so the relief is 0.00 and nothing can be booked, instead of 6.12 against the fee.
No user hint: user_scenario raises only authorizing the credit check on the pending increase request; it names no fee, no draw, no return, no replacement payment and no relief, and gives no hint that anything must be sorted first. The bank accounts (old one closed, new one current) are given only when the agent asks about them, and the only reference to corrections is a passive reaction ('If the representative tells you that something on your line has to be booked or put right before the request can be decided, you tell them to go ahead') triggered by the agent's own explanation.
Tools do not block: task_tools.py: authorize_limit_increase_21546d5b only updates the request (decision_status, approved_limit, decision_date) and credit_limit; assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d and assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c each create one ledger entry and adjust outstanding_balance; grant_returned_fee_relief_6fbb0f32 creates one waiver entry and lowers outstanding_balance. None reads another entry, checks a status, a balance or a prior write, or returns an error; each writes faithfully whether or not any prerequisite is resolved.

FOUR-POINT TEST OF EACH PREREQUISITE SENTENCE (own-rule sentence, ordering connective, record-visible state, one write of this difficulty brings it about). LI <- R: "The approved limit is fixed only after every returned payment on the line whose return code carries a fee shows its returned-payment fee entry." is in the increase rule, uses "only after", names the record state (a fee entry related to each fee-bearing return), and only assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d creates it. LI <- D: "The approved limit is not fixed until each draw on the line carries a draw-fee entry, wherever the tier charges a draw fee." - same four points, only assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c creates a draw-fee entry for a past draw, and that entry enters the draw charges the draw-intensity share reads. LI <- RELIEF: "The approved limit is fixed only after the returned-payment fee of a return that has a replacement payment recorded against it carries a courtesy fee-waiver entry." - "only after", a record state (a courtesy waiver tied to that fee), and only grant_returned_fee_relief_6fbb0f32 books a waiver against a returned-payment fee (the workout relief books against late fees only); the relief paragraph makes that waiver due without a request once the fee is booked on a replaced return. RELIEF <- R: "Replacement relief is fixed only after the returned payment it is for carries its returned-payment fee entry." - only assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d books that fee. All four edges are state form; no action-form fallback was needed. No status registration, persona line or tool order stands in for a real-world event: the return, the replacement payment and the loan return are seeded facts dated before the call.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. line_returned_payment_fee_assessed: line_evt_payments_and_fees, no structured gate applies (payable_status covers payments, late_fee_grace covers late fees) -> policy_scope. line_draw_fee_assessed: line_evt_draws line_active, retired for a back-billed fee by the draw-fee overwrite (and the line is active anyway). line_fee_waived: line_evt_fee_waiver once_per_fee (dedup on related_txn_id: the fee of step 9 has no waiver; a second call would be a duplicate); courtesy_count and courtesy_window are restated by the overwrite shared with the workout relief (granted without a request, still only while fewer than 1 courtesy waiver in 12 months - the line has none - and within 60 days of the fee - booked today). line_limit_changed: line_evt_limit_changes active_line (status active, evidence credit_lines.status) and seasoning (time; positive case 2026-10-16 is 40 months after 2023-06-14; negative case 2023-12-13 is 5 months 29 days, refused; boundary 2023-12-14 inclusive). The base increase conditions are met: no minimum paid 30 or more days late in 12 months (the February minimum was paid 13 days late, the September one was replaced 9 days after its due date), no other increase request in 6 months, hard inquiry authorized by the borrower.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target key credit_line_id b2db4d01-9c63-44e2-8662-5e6f9185e430. Ledger rows included: every line_transactions row of this line (draws, draw fees, interest, annual fees, payments, the return 60288959-05fb-453e-bd13-8d2cfbb8c673, the replacement 7d9789f9-4f17-4b7f-bc38-e1b6e9c1960c, the late fee 410c7a65-39b4-4545-a613-51b8914dc79f). Objects already settled: every draw before 2026-09-10 carries its fee; the 2026-02-14 late fee was booked and paid; the loan fee of 2026-09-16 was paid on 2026-09-20 and never waived. Excluded: nothing on another line (the customer has one line).

SEED ROLES. credit_lines row: tier, limit, age, balance, minimum due. Draw rows: the 12-month draw count (frequent drawer), the 3-month draw charges (draw intensity of the increase), the size of the fee-less draw. Return row: the fee and the relief. Replacement payment (related to the return): timing and cover shares. Late fee 2026-02-28: the late-history share of the relief and the payment-record points of the back-billed draw fee (12 months). Request row: the request reference and the requested-limit cap. Loan row and loan ledger: the exposure share (principal 9,601.14) and the 2026-09-16 loan return and fee (shared-event share of the fee, bank-event basis of the relief). Bank accounts: the closed 4120 account explains the R02 code; 4307 paid the replacement.

PERSONA. Opening: wants to okay the credit check on the increase he requested in the app. On request: mobile, date of birth, ZIP (SSN last four and email as extras), the 9,500 he asked for, the two bank accounts. Passive reactions: lets the agent book whatever must be put right; accepts the hard inquiry; declines AutoPay today; carries out the authorization with the values read to him. Every action is reachable in one call and every must-ask item is in the persona.

DIFFICULTY. The agent must find in the increase paragraph that three ledger items gate the decision, discover that the relief is due without a request and must follow the fee, apply five tiered factors in each of four computations (four methods that change the shape of the formula: the larger of the flat fee and a percent of a large return, the full percent on the first 500.00 and half on the rest for a frequent drawer against the percent above a fee-free portion against the whole draw, the relief basis capped at the flat fee when the loan fee for the same bank event stands, and the graduated increase percent on a limit of 7,500 or more), and hand the final step to the customer.

user_scenario:
You are Desmond Okafor, 47, a high-school chemistry teacher in Chicago, calling Larkspur on your planning period. Last Friday you asked in the Larkspur app for a higher limit on your FlexLine line of credit, and the app now says the request is waiting for you to authorize a credit check. You open with something like "I put in for a higher limit on my FlexLine last week and the app says it's waiting on me to okay the credit check, so I'd like to get that done today." You are upbeat, a bit hurried, and you talk in short sentences.

You give your details only as the representative asks for them: your mobile number is 3125554871, your date of birth is 1978-11-23 (November 23, 1978), and your ZIP code is 60614. If they need one more, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 4639 and your email is desmond.okafor@outlook.com. You don't know reference numbers by heart. If they ask how much you asked for, you remember putting 9,500 in the app. If they ask about your bank accounts, your old Lakeshore Community Bank checking ending in 4120 was closed in September and your current account is the Midwest Heritage Bank checking ending in 4307. You don't remember your balance and leave it to their system.

You do not know Larkspur's rules and you don't guess at them. If the representative tells you that something on your line has to be booked or put right before the request can be decided, you tell them to go ahead; you don't ask for the details of each entry and you don't bring up any charge yourself. You understand the credit check is a hard inquiry and you are fine with it. If they ask whether you want AutoPay turned back on, you say not today, you'll set it up in the app later.

Authorizing the credit check is something you do yourself, so when the representative hands you that step, you carry it out with the line reference, the request reference and the limit exactly as they read them to you, and then you read back what you see. You accept whatever limit they say came out of the review; you never suggest a figure of your own and you don't argue. Once you see the request shown as approved with your new limit, you thank them and hang up.
